raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Cancelling an async caller does not stop a blocking media download. The caller used to release its semaphore permit while that download was still running, so later requests could exceed the download limit. Rejecting a sibling source has the same problem.

## Changes

Move the permit into the blocking fetch closure. The download keeps its slot until it returns or unwinds. A live request can still use any remaining slot. The limit and download timeouts stay the same.

The branch now includes current main and keeps the move of the prefetch code into `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/prefetch.rs`. Start with `fetch_ordered`.

## Tests

Both new regressions use real HTTP downloads with explicit start and release signals. They cover caller cancellation and a failed sibling source, check that a live request can make progress, and check that all permits return after the download finishes.

On the updated branch, restoring permit ownership to the async caller makes both regressions fail. Keeping the permit in the blocking closure makes all 10 prefetch tests pass.

Strict Clippy passes for the workspace, server library and test targets, optional multimodal features, and radix tree. Formatting and matching precommit hooks pass.

These checks ran on macOS ARM64 with Rust 1.92. No GPU inference test or complete server test suite was run for this update.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

Lint passes. Could you rerun the failed jobs in run 38314826017 and merge once the required checks pass? I tried the rerun API, but it returned 403. Thanks!

Hi @rainj-me, I checked the latest run for the approved commit 2774384. The B200 shard failed during the CI health check because GitHub's jobs API returned 502, before the tests ran:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38338508060/job/115220934244

Other jobs are still failed or queued, so I have not confirmed that every remaining failure is infrastructure related. Could you help rerun the affected jobs and check the remaining merge gate? The focused Rust server reruns passed. Thank you!

Independent CPU validation of `5da2b6be7a9b` on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.92.0 (with Codex assistance):

- `cargo +1.92.0 test -p sglang-server --lib frontend::prefetch::tests --locked --offline`: **10 passed**.
- Negative control: retained this PR's tests and semaphore-injection seam, but restored the parent's async-side permit ownership. Exactly the two new regressions failed: `available_permits()` was 2 instead of 1 while the download was still active. The other 8 tests passed. Restoring the fix returned all 10 tests to green.

The tests cover caller cancellation and sibling-fetch failure, plus live-request progress on the remaining slot and eventual permit return. Moving the permit into the blocking closure gives it the lifetime of the actual I/O. No blocking findings in the changed code.

Validation scope: the focused prefetch tests and surrounding fetch/call paths; no full-server or GPU inference run.
